Adoption is more likely when value-when-right is higher, probability of success is higher, and cost-when-wrong is lower. Adoption looks mysterious when treated as a single reliability score. Speaker assertion from the July 2025 talk; not independently measured here. Harrison Chase / LangChain, AI Engineer 2025

Raising value also means shifting interaction patterns from fast RAG/Q&A copilots toward long-running deep research and ambient agents that do more work in the background. Five-second Q&A copilots cap the value an agent can create. Shift UX to long-running deep research and ambient background work. Enterprise and general agent deployment decisions as framed in this talk. Speaker assertion from the July 2025 talk; not independently measured here. Harrison Chase / LangChain, AI Engineer 2025

Context engineering is how you get the most out of today's models by managing the context window, rather than waiting for smarter models to fix brownfield failure. Teams conclude coding agents cannot handle complex or brownfield work. Better tokens in yield better tokens out because the model is stateless. Any coding-agent loop where the next tool call is chosen from conversation state. Does not claim a specific model or harness is sufficient by itself. Dex Horthy / HumanLayer, AI Engineer Code Summit 2025

Intentional compaction—compressing the current window into a reviewed, tagged markdown file and starting a new agent—lets the next run skip rediscovery. Naive re-steering fills the window with search, edits, logs, and MCP JSON until quality collapses. Hand the next agent exact files, line numbers, and the current goal instead of the raw trajectory. Whether the current session is on track or not. Compaction quality still depends on human review of the markdown. Dex Horthy / HumanLayer, AI Engineer Code Summit 2025

Successful agents so far concentrate on high-value work such as Harvey in legal and research/summarization in finance, because people already pay a lot for those tasks. Low-value tasks cannot pay for agent error and operating cost. Choose work people already pay a lot for (legal, investment research). Enterprise and general agent deployment decisions as framed in this talk. Speaker assertion from the July 2025 talk; not independently measured here. Harrison Chase / LangChain, AI Engineer 2025

Connecting offline and online evals creates a flywheel: filter production logs, add spans back to datasets, and improve the next offline run. Offline tests drift from real user traffic. Human review or user-feedback filters select production rows; those rows are appended to eval datasets. Any team that logs production traces with the same span shape as offline cases. Business claims (cut dev time, higher quality) are speaker-attributed, not independently measured here. Doug Guthrie / Braintrust, AI Engineer World's Fair 2025

Frequent intentional compaction means building the entire workflow around keeping the window small and staying in the smart zone. One-off compaction is not enough for hard brownfield work. Research, then plan, then implement, compacting at each phase. Hard problems and multi-repo features; button-color changes do not need the full loop. RPI is a convenient cadence, not a sacred acronym; the durable idea is compaction. Dex Horthy / HumanLayer, AI Engineer Code Summit 2025
